paragraphs: Decision center: the work of Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors is to turn these front-end conditions — students' and clients' abilities and interests and needs and backgrounds, academic and further study and employment and financial aid information, counseling and assessment methods and professional ethics, and the resources and rules of schools and institutions and employers and families — into executable, reviewable and accountable guidance and counseling results: first determine the guidance and counseling and assessment objectives by client needs and professional ethics, then conduct individual and group counseling and career planning and explain assessment results, then assist with course selection and further study and employment and financial aid applications and follow up on implementation, and during that period collaborate with teachers and parents and employers and institutions and keep records and confidentiality and referrals, then carry out programs and lectures and crisis intervention and advocacy, and finally improve services based on data and feedback and complete handover. The focus of judgment is not "being articulate", but whether, along the chain of "assessment—counseling and planning—collaboration and records and referral", one can hold four things — professional ethics, confidentiality boundaries, client interests and verifiable evidence — and leave a checkable record at every step.

Worth trying first: being willing to listen and to be responsible for the client's growth and choices and to accept questioning from students and parents and teachers and institutions; being able to switch pace among counseling and assessment and paperwork and coordination and activities; being willing to act according to professional ethics and confidentiality and the rules and to handle crises and complaints and referrals; and being able to accept the long hours of interviews and lectures driven by semester and application season and examination and assessment and appraisal cycles.

Think carefully: if you expect this job to be just giving answers, or to be only about assessment with no companionship or follow-up, or you are unwilling to act according to professional ethics and confidentiality and the rules and procedures, or you avoid responsibility for crises and confidentiality and client interests, or you treat one assessment or one experience as a conclusion and make major decisions on that basis, or you find it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under high emotion and multi-party pressure, then the actual experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk check: using the fictional client materials and anonymous assessment and application data provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of "writing the counseling objectives for an academic and career guidance interview, plus assessment interpretation, plus action steps, plus a confidentiality and referral check", verifying only whether you are willing to check items one by one against objectives and data and ethics and to honestly mark uncertainty. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not constitute a psychological diagnosis or medical or legal or employment conclusion, and is not equivalent to a counselor license or supervisory qualification.

Decision center: whether client needs and assessment and academic and employment data can be turned into guidance and counseling results that clients and parents and teachers and institutions can all take up and review.

The work rhythm is jointly determined by semester and application season and examination and assessment and appraisal points and project cycles; interviews and paperwork and lectures and coordination are numerous, there is considerable emotional load and multi-party communication, and records and confidentiality need to be documented.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 21-1012.00 Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors. Adjacent occupations — school psychologists (19-3034), social and community service managers (11-9151), rehabilitation counselors (21-1015), substance abuse and mental health counselors (21-1018), marriage and family therapists (21-1013), education administrators, kindergarten through secondary (11-9032), education teachers, postsecondary (25-1081), and training and development managers (11-3131) — have different objects and authorizations; this occupation is not equivalent to a clinical psychology or medical diagnosis post. Practice qualifications and supervision and confidentiality requirements follow the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and industry ethics codes and institutional rules, are not inferred from job titles, and no one may issue medical or psychological or legal conclusions externally beyond authorization.

You can use AI as a controlled aid for information retrieval and paperwork and data, but you cannot treat generated content as unreviewed assessment interpretation or counseling advice or crisis response plans; client information and records and referrals and external communication remain the responsibility of named counselors and supervisors and institutions.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can take responsibility for the client's growth and choices, whether you can act according to professional ethics and confidentiality and data, whether you can communicate under high emotion and multi-party pressure and escalate and refer according to the rules, and whether you are clear about the boundaries of your authority over assessment and counseling and records and external communication; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of "liking to chat" or "being patient"; all of this must be confirmed in supervised counseling and guidance internship experience.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real decisions about counseling and assessment and crisis intervention and referral and records must be undertaken by personnel who hold the appropriate qualifications and act in accordance with the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and industry ethics codes and institutional rules; individuals may not issue medical or psychological or legal conclusions externally beyond their authorization, and this page does not constitute any medical or psychological or legal or employment advice.

The work object of this occupation is students and clients, with high-frequency interaction with multiple parties: abilities and interests and needs and backgrounds, academic and further study and employment and financial aid information, counseling and assessment methods and professional ethics, the resources and rules of schools and institutions and employers and families, and interview and lecture and program and crisis and referral arrangements. The output is guidance and counseling results that meet client interests and professional ethics requirements: individual and group counseling and career planning carried out according to needs and ethics, assessment interpretation and guidance plans formed from data, interview and follow-up and record and confidentiality and referral records completed according to the rules, lecture and activity and evaluation materials completed according to the project, and reviewable service and outcome records. The basis for judgment is client interests and professional ethics and data and institutional rules, not personal preference or job title.

Judgment one: whether client needs align with the counseling and assessment objectives — whether guidance and counseling objectives are determined by needs and ethics and assessment data, rather than giving advice by impression.

Judgment two: whether counseling and assessment implementation are evidence-based — whether they are carried out and explained according to counseling theory and assessment tools and ethics requirements, rather than by personal experience.

Judgment three: whether interviews and follow-up and records and confidentiality follow the rules — whether records and confidentiality and follow-up are kept and documented according to professional ethics and institutional rules, rather than disclosed or omitted at will.

Judgment four: whether further study and employment and financial aid information is accurate — whether it is checked against the latest policies and institution and employer information, rather than by old experience or guessing.

Judgment five: whether collaboration and referral and crisis handling are upheld — whether collaboration with parents and teachers and institutions is carried out according to the rules and crises are assessed and referred according to the process, rather than handled alone or delayed.

Judgment six: whether the boundaries of data and compliance and external communication and conclusions are upheld — whether information is used according to laws and regulations and data authority and privacy and client record requirements, without issuing medical or psychological or legal or employment conclusions externally beyond authorization, and seeking instructions and reporting according to the rules when something is abnormal.

Environment and rhythm: mainly schools and institutional offices and counseling rooms and classrooms and online, with high-frequency communication with students and parents and teachers and institutions; the rhythm is driven by semester and application season and examination and assessment and appraisal points, and interviews and paperwork and lectures and coordination are numerous; specific arrangements and hours follow the institution and jurisdiction.

The work of Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first category is assessment and counseling and planning: assess students' and clients' abilities and interests and needs and backgrounds, conduct individual and group counseling and career planning, explain assessment results and help form academic and further study and employment and financial aid and life plans, assist with course selection and applications and interviews and job search preparation, and follow up on implementation and adjust plans. The second category is collaboration and records and referral: collaborate with teachers and parents and employers and institutions and agencies, maintain interview and follow-up and confidentiality and referral records, handle confidentiality and informed consent and exceptions according to the rules and ethics, and assess and refer and report crises and high-risk situations according to the process. The third category is programs and advocacy and professional development: design and implement lectures and courses and programs and activities and evaluate their effects, carry out prevention and advocacy and resource connection, take part in supervision and training and professional development and comply with practice qualification and ethics requirements, and keep good records and handover of services and outcomes. All three work areas proceed within client interests, professional ethics, data and institutional rules.

Core purpose

To turn client needs and assessment and academic and employment data into executable and reviewable and accountable guidance and counseling results: clear objectives, evidence-based counseling and assessment, accurate information, collaboration and records and referral according to the rules, and external conclusions that hold their boundaries.

Core purposes of adjacent roles: school psychologists safeguard students' psychological and learning support and intervention; social and community service managers safeguard service programs and institutional operations; rehabilitation counselors help people with disabilities and rehabilitation clients find employment and adapt; substance abuse and mental health counselors provide addiction and mental health treatment; marriage and family therapists address family and relationship issues; primary and secondary education administrators safeguard school running and teaching; higher education education teachers conduct teaching and research.
Main objects and basis

The objects are client abilities and interests and needs and backgrounds, academic and further study and employment and financial aid information, counseling and assessment methods and professional ethics, the resources and rules of schools and institutions and employers and families, and interview and lecture and program and crisis and referral arrangements; the basis is client interests and professional ethics and data and institutional rules.

Individual and group counseling and career planning carried out according to needs and ethics, assessment interpretation and guidance plans formed from data, interview and follow-up and record and confidentiality and referral records completed according to the rules, lecture and activity and evaluation materials completed according to the project, and reviewable service and outcome records.

Responsible party

This occupation is responsible for providing counseling and guidance and records according to client interests and professional ethics and data and for confidentiality and referral and client safety; supervisors and institutions and the profession and competent authorities bear management responsibility for practice qualifications and ethics and compliance and conclusions according to laws and regulations and institutional rules.

Responsibility of adjacent roles: borne by the heads of each institution and the relevant professionals according to their respective laws and regulations and ethics and institutional rules, on different bases of authorization.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with clients and parents and teachers and employers and institutions and agencies and medical and social work staff and supervisors, adjusting priorities according to semester and application season and examination and assessment points; crises and confidentiality exceptions and over-authorization matters are escalated and reported and referred according to the rules.

Collaboration of adjacent roles: with teachers and parents and medical staff (school psychologists); with community and civil affairs and health authorities (social and community service managers); with medical and rehabilitation staff and employers (rehabilitation counselors); with medical and social work and judicial staff (addiction and mental health); with families and social workers and medical staff (marriage and family therapists); with teachers and parents and supervisors (primary and secondary schools); with departments and research teams (higher education teachers).
Conclusion boundaries

Must determine counseling and assessment objectives according to client interests and ethics and data, must implement and explain according to counseling theory and assessment tools and ethics, must record and keep confidentiality and follow up according to professional ethics and institutional rules, must check further study and employment information against the latest policies and institution and employer information, must collaborate and refer according to the rules with parents and teachers and institutions, must use client information according to data authority and privacy, and must not issue medical or psychological or legal or employment conclusions externally beyond authorization.

The boundaries of adjacent roles are determined by their own objects and laws and regulations and ethics and institutional rules; similar institutions or job titles do not mean interchangeable duties.
In this work, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be checked?

Common errors cluster in four categories: first, client needs are disconnected from the counseling and assessment objectives, leading to guidance inconsistent with client needs and wasted resources; second, clients are assessed by impression rather than assessment and counseling and data, leading to distorted advice and harm to clients; third, interviews and follow-up and records and confidentiality are not handled according to professional ethics and the rules, leading to privacy breaches and risks to trust and legal exposure; fourth, further study and employment information is outdated, or collaboration and referral and crisis handling do not follow the process, leading to misleading advice and safety and accountability risks. The way to check is that each item has a reviewable basis: needs assessment and counseling and assessment objectives and guidance plans, assessment interpretation and counseling and interview records, interview and follow-up and confidentiality and referral records, further study and employment and financial aid information and sources, and crisis and referral and reporting records — not memory or verbal agreement.

Observation signal one: willing to listen and to be responsible for the client's growth and choices and to accept questioning from students and parents and teachers and institutions, and able to act according to client interests and professional ethics and data rather than by feeling.

Observation signal two: willing to act according to the rules for client data and assessment and counseling and confidentiality and informed consent, and confirming before acting where confidentiality exceptions and referral and crisis and external communication are involved.

Observation signal three: able to stay careful about objectives and ethics and procedures under high emotion and multi-party pressure and application season and assessment cycles, and not skip checks because of schedule pressure.

Observation signal four: able to accept the long hours of interviews and lectures driven by semester and application season and examination and assessment and appraisal cycles, and willing to do records and confidentiality and referral and handover.

Trainable capabilities include needs assessment and counseling and interviewing and listening, use of assessment tools and interpretation of results, career and further study and employment information and planning, confidentiality and informed consent and ethics and referral, crisis identification and handling and resource connection, programs and lectures and activities and effect evaluation, and client data and privacy and records.

Workload includes mainly schools and institutional offices and counseling rooms and classrooms and online with high-frequency communication with students and parents and teachers and institutions; the rhythm is driven by semester and application season and examination and assessment and appraisal points, and interviews and paperwork and lectures and coordination are numerous, with a high emotional load.

Counter-signals include expecting to just give answers, or to be only about assessment with no companionship or follow-up, or being unwilling to act according to professional ethics and confidentiality and the rules and procedures, or avoiding responsibility for crises and confidentiality and client interests, or treating one assessment or one experience as a conclusion and making major decisions on that basis, or finding it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under high emotion and multi-party pressure.

values: Fictional materials

1 set of fictional client background and academic and career materials and institutional rules, 1 set of anonymous assessment and application and employment data and data dictionary, templates for needs assessment and counseling and assessment interpretation and confidentiality and informed consent and referral and crisis and abnormality reporting, and 3 guidance and ethics hazard items.
All materials are fictional and contain no real client information or information unrelated to you.
Work task

Within 40 minutes, write the counseling objectives for an academic and career guidance interview and assessment interpretation and action steps and a confidentiality and referral check, and fill out one form for interviews and follow-up and referral and abnormality reporting.

Do only paper design and checking, without touching real client or assessment data, without making psychological or medical or legal or employment conclusions, and this is not equivalent to a practice qualification or supervision authorization.
Reference result

Counseling objectives are expressed in observable and assessable terms and include a client needs basis; guidance steps include information and resources and time and responsible persons; assessment interpretation includes boundaries and uncertainty; confidentiality and referral include informed consent and exceptions and resources and reporting items.
The reference result is for self-checking and is not the only correct answer.
Boundary statement

The exercises are for career exploration and do not constitute practice qualification, post appointment or supervision authorization; real decisions about counseling and assessment and crisis intervention and referral and records must be undertaken by personnel who hold the appropriate qualifications and act in accordance with the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and industry ethics codes and institutional rules.

items.title: Entry case material: one fictional academic and career guidance interview check

values: Day 1: understand the materials
Read the fictional client materials and anonymous assessment and application data and institutional materials, circle uncertain items and write out a question list.
Day 2: needs and objectives
Lay out counseling and assessment and guidance objectives by client needs and mark items to be confirmed.
Day 3: counseling and interpretation
Write a section of counseling and assessment interpretation and action step notes based on assessment and interview data.
Day 4: information and planning
Write key points for a further study or employment and financial aid plan based on the latest policies and institution and employer sources.
Day 5: confidentiality and referral
Fill out one form for interviews and follow-up and confidentiality and informed consent and referral and crisis and abnormality reporting.
Day 6: timed repeat
Redo it under time limits and record energy and error types.
Day 7: compare and decide
Compare the two versions and write down continue / be cautious / stop and the reasons.

entries: Day 1 judgment: whether the uncertain items in the materials were honestly marked, rather than filled in by guessing.
Day 2 judgment: whether counseling and assessment and guidance objectives were checked against client needs and ethics and data, rather than by impression.
Day 3 judgment: whether the counseling and assessment interpretation notes were written clearly according to ethics and boundaries and uncertainty.
Day 4 judgment: whether further study and employment and financial aid information was checked against the latest policies and sources and the source date marked.
Day 5 judgment: whether the confidentiality and informed consent and referral and crisis and data items are verifiable.
Day 6 judgment: whether confidentiality and informed consent and client interests and professional boundaries can still be upheld under time limits.
Day 7 judgment: take the performance on both versions together and judge whether you are willing to keep investing in educational guidance and career counseling.

subject.summary: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors (United States side O*NET-SOC 21-1012.00, Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors) is a guidance and counseling post in schools and institutions and agencies: providing students and job seekers with academic and career and further study and employment guidance and counseling and assessment and planning; the work includes assessing students' and clients' abilities and interests and needs and backgrounds, providing individual and group counseling and career planning, explaining assessment results and helping form academic and further study and employment and financial aid and life plans, assisting with course selection and applications and interviews and job search preparation, collaborating with teachers and parents and employers and institutions and agencies, maintaining interview and follow-up and confidentiality and referral records, handling confidentiality and informed consent and exceptions according to ethics, assessing and referring and reporting crises and high-risk situations according to the process, designing and implementing lectures and courses and programs and activities and evaluating their effects, carrying out prevention and advocacy and resource connection, and taking part in supervision and training and professional development. United States basis: BLS 2025 wage data median 64,330 USD per year (30.93 USD per hour; that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 376,300, a 2024—2034 projection of "average (Average, 3% to 4%)" and about 31,000 projected openings for 2024—2034 (total for the projection period); the preparation level is Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), the interest code is SCE, and there are 35 tasks; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook separately gives growth of 3% and an average of about 27,800 openings per year on the 2025—2035 basis. Mainland China basis: the qualifications and training and supervision for posts related to school mental health education and career guidance follow the relevant provisions of education administrative departments and institutions, and where teaching and education work is involved the corresponding teaching qualification should be obtained in accordance with the Teachers Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications; this occupation is not equivalent to a clinical psychology or medical diagnosis post. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage basis corresponding to this occupation, and this page preserves the gap faithfully, with the industry average wage serving only as a visible industry proxy.
